hook_text: South Africa's economy GREW for ten years. So why is the average person poorer?
clip_script: Let the economy be the potjie at your family's year-end braai. Growth means exactly one thing: this year's pot has more food in it than last year's pot. Now hold South Africa up to the braai. For roughly ten years, our pot has grown about one percent a year while the crowd around it has grown about one and a half percent. Bigger pot; smaller plates; the average person slowly worse off. If you master a single fact from this lesson, make it that one — you can now explain the national mood at any dinner table using nothing but a pot and a headcount.
visual_style: A cast-iron potjie over coals slowly swelling while more and more chairs crowd around it, plates shrinking in overhead shots, ending on one plate half empty.
mood: Warm braai-smoke familiarity that lands a cold, clarifying fact.
pacing: Relaxed open, tightening cuts as the chairs multiply, a still, silent beat on the final plate.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson: real growth, the queue of one hundred, and what redistribution can actually do.
